predecessor_rejoin.R44AS: R44AS already gives a delta*-critical / branchwise-descending parent whose ordinary Davis-Putnam sibling projection rebounds from rank 2 to rank 3. Therefore raw DP sibling merge is not a new candidate.
predecessor_rejoin.R44BM_distinction: R44BM attacks a different compact sibling-specific merge that avoids the p*q resolvent product by replacing the pivot with two activation variables and one OR clause.

domain.input: A normalized CNF G with a pivot variable x occurring in both polarities.
domain.decomposition: G = H union {x OR A_i}_i union {not-x OR B_j}_j, where H contains no x.

candidate_merge.name: TWO_ACTIVATOR_SIBLING_SPLIT_MERGE
candidate_merge.formula: M = H union {not-a OR A_i}_i union {not-b OR B_j}_j union {a OR b}
candidate_merge.interpretation: a activates the x=0 sibling residue; b activates the x=1 sibling residue.

exact_semantics_theorem.statement: exists_{a,b} M is logically equivalent over the remaining original variables to exists_x G; hence SAT(M) iff SAT(G[x=0]) or SAT(G[x=1]) iff SAT(G).
proof: If G[x=0] is satisfied, set a=1,b=0; all A_i residues are enforced and every b-guarded clause is disabled.
If G[x=1] is satisfied, set a=0,b=1 symmetrically.

Conversely, every model of M satisfies a OR b. If a=1 then H and every A_i hold, giving a model of G[x=0]. If a=0 then b=1 and H plus every B_j hold, giving a model of G[x=1]. If both are 1, either sibling is valid.

incidence_matching_theorem.identity_used: For every CNF F, delta*(F)=|C(F)|-nu(I(F)), where I(F) is the clause-variable incidence bipartite graph and nu is maximum matching size.
incidence_matching_theorem.graph_operation: In I(G), split the pivot variable vertex x into two vertices a,b, send former positive-pivot clause incidences to a and former negative-pivot clause incidences to b, and add one new clause vertex c_ab adjacent to a and b.
matching_lower_bound: Take a maximum matching Q of I(G).
If x is unmatched, retain Q and add edge c_ab-a (or c_ab-b), obtaining |Q|+1 edges.
If x is matched to a positive-pivot clause, replace that edge by the corresponding a-edge and add c_ab-b.
If x is matched to a negative-pivot clause, replace it by the corresponding b-edge and add c_ab-a.
vertex_cover_upper_bound: By Konig's theorem choose a minimum vertex cover K of I(G) with |K|=nu(I(G)).
If x is in K, replace x by both a and b. This increases the cover size by one and covers all redistributed pivot incidences plus c_ab.
If x is not in K, every old clause neighbor of x is already in K. Keep K and add c_ab itself; again the cover size increases by one.
Thus I(M) has a vertex cover of size nu(I(G))+1, so nu(I(M)) <= nu(I(G))+1.

R44BD_effect.M5_REPLAY: SAT replay is immediate from a/b; no global L6 promotion is claimed because M2 already fails.

scope_boundary.blocked_class: The exact two-activator sibling merge obtained by splitting the original pivot incidence vertex and adding one activation-OR clause.
not_blocked: multi-output circuits with nontrivial shared internal gates
rank-reducing exact normalization after a different merge
other ranks not based on maximum deficiency

next_admissible_math.question: Can one fixed sibling-specific operator exploit shared semantic structure of the two cofactors to produce an exact polynomial state of rank <=k-1, or can one prove a barrier for one precisely specified next operator class?
next_admissible_math.anti_drift: Another selector/activator/pivot-copy syntax without a genuinely different semantic mechanism is not a new machine.
